description: PR #129, Codex's two reviews of the same six loaders (commits eb662b6 and 24d2025). Two findings: a different failure in each file, on the same two-line code shape.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return empty defaults when optional files are absent**

On a machine that has never imported a profile, `path.read_text()` raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning the documented empty dictionary; the `.get()` fallback only handles a missing key in an existing JSON file. The same defect affects all three loaders in `profiles.py` and all three readers in `bundle.py`, so older bundles lacking optional sections also fail to load. Handle absent files before decoding JSON and return the appropriate empty value (`{}` or `[]`) for each reader.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return empty sections for legacy list-shaped bundle JSON**

When importing a pre-0.3 bundle, the documented bare JSON list decodes to a Python list, so calling `.get()` raises `AttributeError` instead of returning an empty section. This is reproducible with `[]` in all three bundle readers: `read_manifest`, `read_lockfile`, and `read_overrides`. Handle the legacy list layout before accessing object keys, returning `{}` or `[]` as appropriate so these supported bundles can be read.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
